messages:
Jenna (customer): hey, heads up — after our SSO token rotation yesterday, calls to our dedicated/private endpoint started returning 401s. worked fine before. seems like the Authorization header is missing by the time it hits the inference service.
Jenna (customer): example curl (token redacted):
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \"https://dedicated-us-west.example.internal/api/v1/generate\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}'
```
returns 401 with body: `{\"error\":\"unauthorized\"}`. upstream gateway logs show no `auth` header.
Emily (support): thanks — can you confirm this is only on the dedicated VPC endpoint and not on hosted API? also, did you change any LB or proxy config at the same time as the SSO rotation?
Jenna (customer): only dedicated/private. hosted works fine. we rotated the IdP keys and updated the auth service. nothing else on our side.
Emily (support): ok assigning to eng-platform/infra to check gateway behavior. @Raj @Maya can you take a look?
:eyes:
Raj (eng-platform): pinged. first suspicion: LB or Istio ext_authz filter might be configured to use cookie-based auth and has a rewrite/strip rule for Authorization headers. can you paste the gateway envoy/istio config or a snippet of the ext_authz config? especially any `allowed_headers` or `add_request_headers` blocks.
Maya (eng-infra): also, which load balancer are you using in front of the gateway (GCP LB / F5 / ALB)? some LBs rewrite or drop `Authorization` when they see cookie auth or health-checks.
Carlos (eng-sre): if we can get tcpdump from the gateway pod showing the incoming request vs what envoy forwards, that'll prove if header is dropped pre-or-post envoy.
Jenna (customer): we're on a managed F5 in our VPC. attaching the gateway access logs snippet: 
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:09Z] \"POST /api/v1/generate HTTP/1.1\" 401 - \"-\" 0.002
upstream_request_headers: { }
incoming_request_headers: { host: dedicated-us-west.example.internal, cookie: \"sso=...\", authorization: \"Bearer REDACTED\" }
```
looks like upstream_request_headers is empty for auth.
Emily (support): interesting — incoming has Authorization but upstream doesn't. suggests LB or an intermediate proxy is stripping before envoy/istio receives it, or envoy ext_authz is consuming it and not forwarding. Raj/Maya to confirm.
Raj (eng-platform): two quick checks: 1) is Istio configured with `always_forward_or_inject_auth_header` or similar? 2) ext_authz can optionally `remove_headers_on_success` depending on adapter. share ext_authz config please.
Maya (eng-infra): ask customer to hit the gateway pod directly (bypass LB) using curl to pod IP from inside the VPC (if allowed) to see if header reaches service behind envoy.
Jenna (customer): tried that by port-forwarding into the gateway pod from our jump host — direct request to pod IP preserves Authorization and request is accepted. so LB is suspect.
Raj (eng-platform): that rules out envoy ext_authz consuming & not forwarding. sounds like the F5 has an iRule that collapses cookie+auth into a session and strips auth header. common pattern when they convert cookie to header internally. can you share the F5 virtual server rules? any `HTTP::header remove` / `HTTP::header replace` rules?
Jenna (customer): checking with our infra team now — they found an iRule that ran after the SSO change which focuses on migrating tokens into a session cookie and removes the Authorization header. they thought it was safe.
Maya (eng-infra): ok that explains it. for dedicated/private customers we expect gateways to receive Authorization from client. two remediation paths: 1) update F5 to stop removing Authorization (recommended), or 2) have F5 copy the header into `x-forwarded-authorization` instead of removing then update our gateway to accept either header temporarily.
Carlos (eng-sre): for quick repro you can set a request in F5 to add header back: `HTTP::header insert Authorization \"Bearer <session-token>\"` but that's not ideal long term.
Emily (support): customer asked for a minimal temporary workaround we can suggest in docs — maybe instruct them to set the F5 to preserve Authorization for requests to `/api/*` and roll back the iRule.
Jenna (customer): infra has put in a change to stop stripping Authorization. How should we validate with Redwood gateway? any quick tests or logs to confirm end-to-end?
Raj (eng-platform): after change, send the same curl and give us gateway logs. We look for `incoming_request_headers` containing Authorization and `upstream_request_headers` forwarding it. Also check our ext_authz decision logs (should show decision but not remove header). Example debug command for the gateway pod:
```
kubectl logs -n redwood gateway-abc123 -c envoy --since=5m | grep generate -A5 -B2
```
and tcpdump if needed: `tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap port 443` from the pod.
Maya (eng-infra): FYI if you can't edit the F5 immediately, you can temporarily configure a request-transform on the gateway to accept `x-forwarded-authorization` and set it as `Authorization` before the ext_authz call. config snippet (Envoy Lua filter):
```
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local xf = request_handle:headers():get(\"x-forwarded-authorization\")
        if xf ~= nil and request_handle:headers():get(\"authorization\") == nil then
          request_handle:headers():add(\"authorization\", xf)
        end
      end
```
This is a stopgap; prefer LB fix.
Jenna (customer): infra rolled back the iRule and preserved Authorization. re-tested and call succeeds. attaching new gateway log snippet: 
```
incoming_request_headers: { host: dedicated-us-west.example.internal, authorization: \"Bearer REDACTED\" }
upstream_request_headers: { authorization: \"Bearer REDACTED\" }
200 OK
```
Thanks all.
AuthBot: noted change in gateway config for customer-id-42, creating ticket RW-INC-2026 to track audit/patch.
Carlos (eng-sre): leaving follow-ups: 1) confirm no healthcheck or caching layer reintroduces strip, 2) ask infra to add test that hits `/api/*` with Authorization on deploy, 3) consider documenting common LB gotchas in our Dedicated onboarding checklist.
Emily (support): marking as resolved from support side — will keep RW-INC-2026 open until infra confirms stable. :white_check_mark:
Jenna (customer): thanks everyone, appreciate the quick help! :raised_hands:
